A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AVCD research and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. Retained, renumbered, and added material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, decoding ablations, latency measurements, and qualitative examples, including image-model results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds OmniBench results, component ablations, and hallucination-category measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Dominance recognition, attentive masking, trimodal contrastive decoding, entropy-based skipping, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Describing masking as zeroing clarifies implementation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds OmniBench evaluation using video-SALMONN across eight categories, including action, story, object, and contextual understanding. This extends audio-visual benchmark coverage while retaining the existing datasets and modality domains.

E2.justification: OPERA, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator in the new OmniBench comparison, alongside Base, VCD, VCD*, and AVCD. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and sensitivity comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The distortion diagnostic changes from whole-distribution KL divergence to approximation error after plausibility filtering. New evaluations add a FlashAttention-enabled Base configuration and staged component controls starting from random modality dominance. v2 also specifies AVHBench test/validation roles, but v1's unspecified split prevents establishing the exact split change.

E4.justification: New Tables A.2 and A.5 substantially extend the analyses by isolating component contributions to accuracy and latency and separating hallucination types. The main masking diagnostic is replaced with an approximation-error evaluation. Existing dominance, alpha, masking-ratio, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions describe reporting means and standard deviations across multiple runs without specifying run counts or seeds. Changed means and deviations do not establish a change in uncertainty-reporting practice; no new confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Central AVHBench results are replaced: VideoLLaMA2 Base/AVCD accuracy changes from 78.05/81.95 to 70.52/72.15, and video-SALMONN from 60.00/66.83 to 58.19/62.18. Captioning, AVHBench ablation values, and plotted latencies also change; new OmniBench, component, and category results appear. These replacements do not establish same-setting performance deterioration. MUSIC-AVQA, video-QA, and POPE results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Taylor-approximation assumptions, Appendix A derivations, and Appendix B plausibility constraint are unchanged. The new approximation-error measurement changes empirical validation rather than adding or revising a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the stated AVHBench relative improvements from 6%/11% to 2%/7% for VideoLLaMA2/video-SALMONN. The three methodological contributions and broad applicability claims remain unchanged. The earlier VideoLLaMA2 table actually implies approximately 5%, rather than its advertised 6%.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the components as complementary and identifies gains in vision-induced audio errors and audio-visual matching, with no gain in the audio-induced visual category. Efficiency discussion now qualifies comparison with Base as excluding FlashAttention. Appendix H's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit repository URL, clarifies masking as zeroing, and documents AVHBench whole-dataset testing versus initial-release validation and AVCD's non-use of FlashAttention. v1 already mentioned supplied code and a README. Hardware and stated masking, contrastive-weight, entropy, and plausibility hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: FlashAttention-2 and OmniBench are newly cited in connection with efficiency and added evaluation. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning otherwise remain stable; OPERA was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify masking, experimental settings, results, and efficiency; Appendix D gains three subsections. The conference footer replaces the preprint footer. Most prose and the overall main-text and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 4's KL chart becomes v2 Table 1; three appendix tables are added. The speed plot is redrawn with revised axes, markers, and a FlashAttention legend entry, and its unit becomes s/token. Other figures and tables largely retain their design, with resizing, renumbering, and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: The direct approximation-error check, OmniBench comparison, and component and hallucination-category analyses strengthen empirical support, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by inconsistent speed reporting: v2 Figure 5 plots approximately 1.7 versus 1.9 s/token for AVCD at tau=0.8 versus VCD, while the text retains 2.25 versus 2.5. The added evidence and transparency support a limited net improvement.
